title: Reasons for Separate Study of Organic Compounds
notes: **Combustion:** organic compounds burn in air to give $CO_2$ and $H_2O$. Inorganic compounds generally do not burn.
**Low melting and boiling points:** most organic compounds are molecular with weak intermolecular forces, so they melt and boil at relatively low temperatures.
**Insolubility in water, solubility in organic solvents:** organic compounds are generally non-polar or weakly polar, so they dissolve in non-polar solvents like ether, benzene, chloroform.
**Slow reactions:** organic reactions are generally slower than inorganic reactions and often need heat, light or catalysts.
**Isomerism:** same molecular formula can give different structures with different properties. This is rare in inorganic chemistry.
